well_lift_ft.source: Team assumption for Merced area total dynamic lift. User adjustable. Check DWR SGMA Portal well data for a specific farm.

surface_water_price_per_af.source: Merced Irrigation District 2024 rate ($50/af); 2022 drought rate was $100/af

by_region._note: Typical agricultural surface water price per acre-foot by cost region. Rates vary a lot by district and water year; each value is a starting point for the user to adjust. Merced County itself uses the top level 'value' (Merced Irrigation District).

Sacramento Valley.source: Glenn-Colusa Irrigation District 2024 rate sheet: $44.05 per acre fixed plus $9.05/af volumetric (https://www.gcid.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/2024-Water-Rate-Sheet.pdf). About $18/af at 5 af/acre applied.

San Joaquin Valley North.source: Merced Irrigation District 2024 rate ($50/af), same as the Merced value.

San Joaquin Valley South.source: Westlands Water District 2024-25 contract water rate, Areas 1 and 3, adopted June 18, 2024: $150.29/af (https://wwd.ca.gov/water-management/water-rates/). Friant and Kern districts differ.

Central Coast.source: Pajaro Valley Water Management Agency delivered water charge, 2024-25: $392/af, rising to $501/af on July 1, 2025 (https://pajaronian.com/pv-water-board-approves-rate-increase/). Most Central Coast farms pump groundwater instead.

Southern California.source: Imperial Irrigation District agricultural rate, $20/af, unchanged since 2011 (https://legal-planet.org/2025/12/19/eliminate-the-imperial-irrigation-district/). Coastal Southern California (Ventura, San Diego) ag water costs far more.

North Coast.source: No district rate found. Team estimate; most North Coast farms use wells, ponds, or recycled water.

Mountain.source: No district rate found. Team estimate for intermountain and foothill irrigation districts.

price_mode.note: current: latest available price applied to every year. historical: each year's own price.
